subject: humanities
passage: In 1887, the eye doctor L. L. Zamenhof published a plan for Esperanto, a new language that he hoped people from many different countries could learn and share. To make it easy to pick up, he gave it highly ______ rules: every noun ends in -o, every adjective ends in -a, and verbs never change form to match their subjects.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Zamenhof wanted Esperanto to be "easy to pick up." The colon introduces examples of its rules: "every noun" ends the same way, "every adjective" ends the same way, and verbs "never change form." Rules without exceptions are consistent, so "consistent" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Zamenhof wanted the language to be "easy to pick up," and the rules listed are simple patterns with no exceptions, the opposite of confusing.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Zamenhof published his plan so that many people could learn the language; nothing in the text suggests the rules were hidden.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Esperanto was "a new language" published in 1887, so its rules could not be ancient.
explanation.D: Correct. The examples after the colon show rules that work the same way every time ("every noun," "every adjective," verbs that "never change"), which is what "consistent" means.
